On 18 January 2026, a high-speed passenger train derailed in the municipality of Adamuz , in the province of Córdoba , Spain. The derailment occurred on a straight section of the track that was last refurbished in May 2025. [1] A second train crashed into it and was also derailed. The incident killed 46 people and injured 292 others, including 15 in critical condition. [2] The crash was Spain's worst railway disaster since the Santiago de Compostela derailment in 2013, [3] [4] and the fourth deadliest railway accident ever recorded in the country. [5] Background Spain's high-speed rail network is the second longest in the world , behind China's . [6] Fatal derailments have occurred on the network, most notably the Santiago de Compostela derailment in July 2013 that killed 79 people. The Madrid–Seville high-speed rail line has been operational since 1992. [7] Since 2014, the line has been operated by the state-owned infrastructure operator ADIF–Alta Velocidad . [8] Renfe-Operadora , Spain's state-owned national train operator, was created in 2005 as a successor to the long-established Red Nacional de los Ferrocarriles Españoles . [9] ILSA, a rail company majority-owned by Trenitalia , was founded in 2019, [10] and began offering services in Andalusia in 2023 under the brand Iryo .
